# `nish/net/http1-client-codec`

The client side of HTTP/1.1, sans-IO: a request writer and an incremental response parser, bytes in, events and bytes out, and no socket anywhere. `nish/net/http1-codec` is the server side; the event constants and the chunk writers are shared and imported from there.

```ts
import {
  HTTP1_E_BARE_LF,
  HTTP1_E_BODY_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_CHUNK,
  HTTP1_E_CHUNK_LINE_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_CODING,
  HTTP1_E_COUNT_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_FIELD,
  HTTP1_E_FRAMING,
  HTTP1_E_HEADER_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_INFORMATIONAL_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_LENGTH,
  HTTP1_E_NONE,
  HTTP1_E_STATUS_LINE,
  HTTP1_E_STATUS_LINE_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_SWITCH,
  HTTP1_E_TRAILER_LIMIT,
  HTTP1_E_TRUNCATED,
  HTTP1_E_VERSION,
  HTTP1_INFORMATIONAL,
  HTTP1_MAX_CHUNK_LINE,
  HTTP1_MAX_INFORMATIONAL,
  Http1ResponseParser,
  http1RequestHead,
  http1UpgradeRequestHead,
  http1WriteRequestHead,
} from "nish/net/http1-client-codec";
```

```ts
import { HTTP1_NEED_MORE, HTTP1_HEAD, HTTP1_BODY, HTTP1_END, HTTP1_ERROR } from "nish/net/http1-codec";
import { Http1ResponseParser } from "nish/net/http1-client-codec";

const p = new Http1ResponseParser(maxStatusLine, maxHeaderBytes, maxHeaders, maxBody, maxTrailerBytes);
p.expect(false, false);
p.feed(received, 0, n); // and p.finish() when the server closes
let event: i32 = p.next();
while (event !== HTTP1_NEED_MORE) {
  // HTTP1_HEAD: p.status, p.reason, p.header("content-type"), ...
  // HTTP1_BODY: p.body[p.bodyOff .. p.bodyOff + p.bodyLen)
  // HTTP1_ERROR: p.error and p.errorText say why; close
  event = p.next();
}
```

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Http1ResponseParser" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#http1responseparser">

<scalar-callout type="info">

**The writer** is `http1RequestHead`, which answers a request line and
header section with the framing field the body needs, and
`http1WriteRequestHead`, which writes the same head into a caller's buffer
with nothing allocated. A chunked body is written with `http1Chunk` and
`http1LastChunk` from `nish/net/http1-codec`. The writer refuses anything that
would let a caller's string end a line early or frame the body itself — the
request-splitting and request-smuggling shapes. `http1UpgradeRequestHead`
is the one way to ask the server to switch protocols: it writes `Upgrade`
and `Connection: Upgrade` itself, and every other writer refuses a
`Connection` that lists `upgrade`.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="The parser">

**The parser** is a push-pull machine, like the server's. A caller tells it
what it asked (`expect`), `feed`s whatever slice the socket gave it, cut
anywhere, and calls `next()` until it answers `HTTP1_NEED_MORE`:

</scalar-detail>

The events are `HTTP1_INFORMATIONAL` (an interim 1xx response was read; the
final one follows), `HTTP1_HEAD` (the final response's status line and
header section are in), `HTTP1_BODY` (some body bytes, de-chunked),
`HTTP1_END` (the response is complete; with `keepAlive()` the next one
follows), `HTTP1_UPGRADE` (a CONNECT was answered with 2xx, or a request
that `expectUpgrade` named was answered with 101, and the connection is a
tunnel now: `tunnelBytes()` answers what was fed past the head),
`HTTP1_CLOSED` (the connection is done: the server closed it between
responses, or the last response was not kept alive) and
`HTTP1_ERROR`. The last three repeat on every later call. Only complete
lines are acted on, body bytes are counted, never guessed, and every
refusal is decided by the same byte wherever the input was cut, so the
sequence of events, the concatenated body and the error code do not depend
on the split —
`tests/link/net_http1_client` feeds a corpus at every split point.

<scalar-detail title="How a response ends">

**How a response ends** (RFC 9112 §6.3): a response to HEAD, a 1xx, 204 or
304 has no body whatever its fields say; a 2xx to CONNECT is a tunnel; a
`Transfer-Encoding: chunked` response is de-chunked; a `Content-Length`
response is that many bytes; anything else is read until the server closes,
which `finish()` reports. A connection closed anywhere else is
`HTTP1_E_TRUNCATED`, so a cut-short body is never taken for a whole one.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**What it refuses**, each with its own code in `error`: a malformed status
line, an HTTP major version other than 1, a bare LF, a malformed field line
(an obs-fold, whitespace before the colon, a control byte in a value), a 101
to a request that did not ask to switch protocols, `Transfer-Encoding` together
with `Content-Length`, a transfer coding other than one `chunked` or one in
an HTTP/1.0 response, a `Content-Length` that is not a decimal or whose
repeats disagree, a malformed chunk, a status line, header section, field
count, body or trailer section over the caller's limit, a chunk-size line
over `HTTP1_MAX_CHUNK_LINE` and more than `HTTP1_MAX_INFORMATIONAL` interim
responses. Each of these is a response-smuggling or a resource shape, and
each is refused rather than repaired: a client that repairs one differently
from a proxy disagrees with it about where the next response starts. An
error is final.

</scalar-callout>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

Written from RFC 9112 and RFC 9110, not ported from another implementation.

## http1UpgradeRequestHead

A request that asks the server to switch the connection to `upgrade` (RFC
9110 §7.8), such as a WebSocket opening handshake: `http1RequestHead`'s head
with no body, and `Upgrade: <upgrade>` and `Connection: Upgrade` written
after the caller's fields. Answers `null` for everything `http1RequestHead`
refuses, an `upgrade` that is not one token, and an `Upgrade` or
`Connection` among the caller's fields, which would contradict the two this
writes. A response to it is read after `expect(false, false)` and then
`expectUpgrade()`, so that its 101 answers `HTTP1_UPGRADE`.

```ts
function http1UpgradeRequestHead(
  method: string,
  target: string,
  names: string[],
  values: string[],
  upgrade: string,
): u8[] | null
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="method" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="target" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="names" type="string[]" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="values" type="string[]" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="upgrade" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

## http1WriteRequestHead

An HTTP/1.1 request line and header section (RFC 9112 §3, §5), ending in
the empty line, written into `out` at `at` with nothing allocated, and
answers where it ends. `Host` goes first, as RFC 9110 §7.2 asks, then the
caller's other fields in order, then the framing field `bodyLength` asks
for: `Content-Length: n` for `n >= 0`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` for -1
(`HTTP1_CHUNKED`), and neither for -2 (`HTTP1_NO_BODY`).

Answers `HTTP1_REFUSED` for a method that is not a token; a target that is
not a form the method may send (see the guide) or that holds a space, a
control byte, a non-ASCII byte or a `#`; a field name that is not a token or
a value holding CR, LF or another control byte (which would end the line
early and let the rest be read as a field or a second request); `names` and
`values` of different lengths; not exactly one `Host`; a `Content-Length` or
`Transfer-Encoding` among the caller's fields, since the framing is decided
here; a `Connection` that lists `upgrade`, which only
`http1UpgradeRequestHead` may write; and a `bodyLength` below -2. Answers
`HTTP1_NO_ROOM` when it is well formed but does not fit. Either way `out` is untouched.

```ts
function http1WriteRequestHead(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  method: string,
  target: string,
  names: string[],
  values: string[],
  bodyLength: i64,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="method" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="target" type="string" required>
</scalar-field>

## Http1ResponseParser

One connection's response parser: responses on a kept-alive connection
follow one another through the same parser, each after its `expect`.

```ts
class Http1ResponseParser
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1ResponseParser(maxStatusLine: i32, maxHeaderBytes: i32, maxHeaders: i32, maxBody: i64, maxTrailerBytes: i32)` | Each `i32` limit is clamped into 0 to 2^30 and `maxBody` into 0 to 2^53, so that the sums the parser makes of them cannot overflow. |
| `body: u8[]` | The buffer the last `HTTP1_BODY`'s bytes are in, at `bodyOff`, `bodyLen` long. |
| `bodyLen: i32` |  |
| `bodyOff: i32` |  |
| `bodyTotal: i64` | De-chunked body bytes so far, against `maxBody`. |
| `buf: u8[]` | The bytes fed and not yet consumed are `buf[start .. end)`. |
| `chunked: boolean` |  |
| `closed: boolean` | Whether `finish()` said the server closed the connection. |
| `contentLength: i64` | The declared body length, or -1 when the response has none or is chunked or read until close. |
| `end: i32` |  |
| `error: i32` | Why `next()` said `HTTP1_ERROR`: one of the `HTTP1_E_` codes. |
| `errorText: string` | What was wrong, once `next()` said `HTTP1_ERROR`; for a log. |
| `fieldCount: i32` | Field lines of the response so far, its trailers included, against `maxHeaders`. |
| `head: u8[]` | The response's reason phrase and kept fields, copied: `head[reasonStart .. reasonEnd)` is the reason, and field `i` is `head[spans[4i] .. spans[4i + 1])`, its name in lowercase, then `head[spans[4i + 2] .. spans[4i + 3])`, its value. Both arrays are reused from response to response. |
| `headUsed: i32` | Bytes of `head` in use, and the fields recorded in `spans`. |
| `informational: i32` | Interim responses before this request's final one, against `HTTP1_MAX_INFORMATIONAL`. |
| `keepStrings: boolean` | Whether `names`, `values` and `reason` are filled; `fieldsAsSpans()` clears it. |
| `left: i64` | Bytes left in a length-delimited body or in the current chunk. |
| `lineEnd: i32` |  |
| `lineStart: i32` | The line `http1ClientTakeLine` found is `buf[lineStart .. lineEnd)`, its CRLF dropped. |
| `maxBody: i64` |  |
| `maxHeaderBytes: i32` |  |
| `maxHeaders: i32` |  |
| `maxStatusLine: i32` |  |
| `maxTrailerBytes: i32` |  |
| `minor: i32` | The minor version: 0 for HTTP/1.0, 1 for HTTP/1.1 and anything above it. |
| `names: string[]` | The field names, in lowercase, in the order they arrived; `values` beside them, OWS trimmed. These and `reason` are filled only while the parser keeps strings, which it does until `fieldsAsSpans()`; `fields()`, `fieldName`, `fieldValue`, `reasonText` and `header` answer in either mode. |
| `persistent: boolean` |  |
| `reason: string` | The reason phrase, which RFC 9112 §4 says a client ignores; for a log. |
| `reasonEnd: i32` |  |
| `reasonStart: i32` |  |
| `scan: i32` | Where the search for the next LF resumes, so a line fed a byte at a time is scanned once. |
| `sectionBytes: i32` | Bytes of the header or trailer section so far, against its limit. |
| `spanCount: i32` |  |
| `spans: i32[]` |  |
| `start: i32` |  |
| `state: i32` |  |
| `status: i32` | The status code of the response last read. |
| `values: string[]` |  |
| `wasConnect: boolean` |  |
| `wasHead: boolean` | What `expect` said of the request this response answers. |
| `wasUpgrade: boolean` | Whether `expectUpgrade` said the request asked to switch protocols. |
| `buffered(): i32` | How many bytes were fed and not consumed yet. |
| `expect(methodWasHead: boolean, wasConnect: boolean): void` | Says what the request this response answers was: a response to HEAD has no body, and a 2xx to CONNECT is a tunnel. It takes effect only while the parser waits for a response's first status line, and the parser forgets it after that response's `HTTP1_END`; anywhere else it does nothing, so a pipelining caller says it once per response, after the last one's end. |
| `expectUpgrade(): void` | Says the request this response answers asked to switch protocols (it was written by `http1UpgradeRequestHead`), so a 101 is that switch: the parser answers `HTTP1_HEAD` with its status and fields readable, `HTTP1_END`, and then `HTTP1_UPGRADE`, and `tunnelBytes()` answers what was fed past the head. Any other status is read as it would be without it. It is said after `expect`, which clears it, and like `expect` it takes effect only while the parser waits for a response's first status line. Without it a 101 is refused with `HTTP1_E_SWITCH`: a server may not switch a connection whose client never asked. |
| `feed(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Appends `data[off .. off + len)` to the input. A window outside `data` panics. After `finish()`, or once the parser has closed or refused, the input is dropped; in a tunnel it is kept for `tunnelBytes()`. |
| `fieldName(i: i32): string` | Field `i`'s name, in lowercase, as a fresh string; "" past the last field. |
| `fields(): i32` | How many fields the response last read has; trailers are not kept. |
| `fieldsAsSpans(): void` | Stops filling `names`, `values` and `reason`, which then stay empty: a response's fields are read through `fields()`, `fieldName`, `fieldValue`, `reasonText` and `header`, which make a string only when asked. A parser kept for many responses allocates nothing per response this way. |
| `fieldValue(i: i32): string` | Field `i`'s value, OWS trimmed, as a fresh string; "" past the last field. |
| `finish(): void` | Says the server closed the connection: a body read until close ends there, a parser waiting for a response with nothing fed is closed, and anything else is `HTTP1_E_TRUNCATED` once the bytes fed before it are read. |
| `header(name: string): string \| null` | The value of the first field named `name` (any case), or `null`. |
| `keepAlive(): boolean` | Whether the connection may carry the next request once this response has ended (RFC 9112 §9.3): a 1.1 response unless `Connection` lists `close`, a 1.0 response only when it lists `keep-alive`, and never one read until close, a tunnel or an error. |
| `next(): i32` | The next event the input holds; see the module comment. |
| `reasonText(): string` | The reason phrase, as a fresh string. |
| `reset(): void` | Makes the parser as it was new, for the next connection, keeping its limits, its mode and its buffers: what was fed and not read is dropped, and an error or a close is forgotten. |
| `tunnelBytes(): u8[]` | In a tunnel: every byte fed past the response head, as a fresh array. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="4,096" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_MAX_CHUNK_LINE: i32`

The longest chunk-size line, extension included, the parser reads.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="32" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_MAX_INFORMATIONAL: i32`

The most interim 1xx responses the parser reads before a final one.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_BARE_LF: i32`

`error`: a line ended in a LF without its CR (RFC 9112 §2.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="14" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_BODY_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: a declared or a received body longer than `maxBody`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_CHUNK: i32`

`error`: a malformed chunk size, chunk extension or chunk terminator (RFC 9112 §7.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_CHUNK_LINE_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: a chunk-size line longer than `HTTP1_MAX_CHUNK_LINE`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_CODING: i32`

`error`: a transfer coding list that is not one `chunked`, or one in an HTTP/1.0 response.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="13" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_COUNT_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: more fields, trailers included, than `maxHeaders`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_FIELD: i32`

`error`: a malformed field line: an obs-fold, a bad name, whitespace before the colon, a control byte.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_FRAMING: i32`

`error`: both `Transfer-Encoding` and `Content-Length` (RFC 9112 §6.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="12" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_HEADER_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: a header section longer than `maxHeaderBytes`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="17" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_INFORMATIONAL_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: more than `HTTP1_MAX_INFORMATIONAL` interim responses.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_LENGTH: i32`

`error`: a `Content-Length` that is not a run of digits, or values that differ (a value past 2^53 differs from any).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_NONE: i32`

`error`: nothing is wrong.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_STATUS_LINE: i32`

`error`: the status line is not `HTTP/1.x`, a three-digit status from 100 to 599 and an optional reason.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_STATUS_LINE_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: a status line longer than `maxStatusLine`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_SWITCH: i32`

`error`: a 101 to a request that did not ask to switch protocols (see `expectUpgrade`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="15" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_TRAILER_LIMIT: i32`

`error`: a trailer section longer than `maxTrailerBytes`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_TRUNCATED: i32`

`error`: the connection closed before the response ended.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_E_VERSION: i32`

`error`: the response's HTTP major version is not 1.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_INFORMATIONAL: i32`

`next()`: an interim 1xx response was read; `status` and the fields are its.

</scalar-card>
